questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram and M is the midpoint of diagonal AC. Explain, using the 180° rotation about M, why AB = CD and AD = CB.
questions.prompt_markup: ABCD is a parallelogram and M is the midpoint of diagonal AC. Explain, using the 180° rotation about M, why AB = CD and AD = CB.
questions.correct_answer: The rotation swaps A and C and sends B to D, so it maps AB onto CD and AD onto CB; rotations keep length.
questions.required_method: Find the images of A, line AB, and line AD; then the image of B as an intersection of lines.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: M is the midpoint of AC, so A ↔ C; a 180° rotation maps line AB to the parallel line through C, which is line CD (parallel postulate), and line CB to the parallel line through A, which is AD; B = AB ∩ CB goes to CD ∩ AD = D; lengths are kept.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a rhombus (a parallelogram with all four sides congruent), with diagonals meeting at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.prompt_markup: ABCD is a rhombus (a parallelogram with all four sides congruent), with diagonals meeting at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.required_method: Use that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, then SSS on triangles AEB and AED (or the perpendicular bisector converse).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: BE = ED (diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other); AB = AD; AE = AE; △AEB ≅ △AED (SSS); ∠AEB ≅ ∠AED form a linear pair, so both are 90°. Alternative: A and C are each equidistant from B and D, so AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD.
